candidates.title: LR/SC reservation is keyed by virtual address, so an SC succeeds on a different physical word after a remap and sfence.vma
candidates.component: Interpreter (main-processor A extension: execute_LR / execute_SC, ilrsc register); the same source is compiled into the uarch program, so the uarch and the regenerated Solidity step implement it identically
candidates.role: Honest operator (interpreter, per the AUDIT.md component table). The uarch program fixed on-chain and the referee verifier share the identical semantics, so there is no divergence between paths
candidates.location: src/interpret.cpp: execute_LR (lines ~1292-1306, `a.write_ilrsc(vaddr)`), execute_SC (lines ~1313-1338, `if (a.read_ilrsc() == vaddr)`); write_csr_satp (~2233-2285) and execute_SFENCE_VMA (~3574-3623) do not touch ilrsc; only set_prv (~380-391) and SC clear it
candidates.description: LR records the *virtual* address of the reserved word in ilrsc, and SC succeeds whenever the SC's virtual address equals ilrsc. The RISC-V A extension says that SC 'succeeds only if the reservation is still valid and the reservation set contains the bytes being written'. A reservation set is a set of memory bytes, which are physical. When the guest changes the translation of the reserved virtual address while it stays at the same privilege level (a satp write or a PTE update followed by sfence.vma, with no trap in between), the next SC to the same virtual address writes a different physical word. It still succeeds and returns 0, even though that word was never reserved. ilrsc is cleared only by SC and by privilege changes (set_prv), never by satp writes or sfence.vma. Aliasing in the opposite direction (LR at V1 and SC at V2, both mapped to the same physical word) fails the SC. Failing is allowed, so that case is not a defect.
candidates.trigger: Guest code in S-mode (or M-mode with MPRV) runs: lr.d x6,(x5); csrw satp,<new root mapping the same VA to another PA> (or a store to the leaf PTE); sfence.vma; sc.d x9,x8,(x5). Any input that takes control of the guest can run this. A correct guest could reach it only if it held a reservation across a remap without a trap.
candidates.reachability: Reachable from any valid template: the instruction sequence uses only guest-writable registers, CSRs and memory, and needs no API call. It is deterministic and identical on every path, because the same interpret.cpp runs natively, in the uarch, and in the replay/Solidity step.
candidates.rating_steps: 1 Out of scope: no. The trigger is guest instructions, which section 8 does not exclude. 2 Role: the interpreter is 'Honest operator' (AUDIT.md: 'Interpreter, state-access layers, devices, uarch program ... | Honest operator'). The uarch program and verifier share the behavior, but there is no divergence. 3 High/Medium cases: the Medium case 'An undocumented deterministic deviation, consistent across all paths, in behavior that no correct guest relies on for isolation or data integrity (R7)' fits under the reading that correct guests never hold a reservation across a same-privilege remap. Linux clears reservations with a dummy SC on every trap return, and kernel LR/SC loops contain no satp write or sfence.vma. Claimed: Medium. 4 Critical (alternative reading): R7 says 'In these areas, any deviation lets an input subvert a correct guest, even a deviation that is consistent across all paths', and lists 'Atomics and fences'. Under that literal reading this violates R7 at a reachable state and would be Critical. The deciding fact is whether any correct guest relies on SC failing after a remap or sfence.vma within one privilege level and without a trap. 5 Low: n/a.
candidates.claimed_severity: Medium (Critical under the literal reading of R7's 'Atomics and fences' clause)
candidates.threat_to_goal: It does not make paths disagree, so no wrong hash or proof follows. It is a deviation from the A-extension semantics in an area R7 singles out ('Atomics and fences'). A guest that relies on SC failing for an unreserved physical word could lose atomicity, for example a lock-free update racing a page migration done without a trap. The atomic update could then land on the wrong page and corrupt guest data, which the threat model counts as data integrity.
candidates.evidence: Ran /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-machine-emulator/549e7dd9-06ba-5ccf-8b17-f8cce9526655/scratchpad/campaign/r1/R7/lrsc.lua against the in-tree build (bugs/env.sh). Setup: Sv39, S-mode, VA 0x1000 mapped to P1 under root A and to P2 under root B. Sequence: lr.d; csrw satp (root B); sfence.vma; sc.d. Output: 'pc=5010 x9(sc result)=0 P1=1111 P2=9999 mcause=0'. The SC succeeded and wrote P2, which was never reserved.
candidates.test_idea: bugs/<ID>/test.lua: build the two page tables as in lrsc.lua. Run 10 mcycles from S-mode, then assert x9 ~= 0 (the SC failed) and that P2 still holds its original value. Optionally add a variant that changes the leaf PTE instead of satp. The test fails (exit 1) on audit/prt2. It passes once the reservation is recorded by physical address (for example, translate in LR and compare in SC), or once ilrsc is invalidated on satp writes and sfence.vma.

candidates.title: Undocumented and incomplete Zcb: compressed encodings that RV64IMAFDC reserves execute, including Zbb/Zba-dependent ones whose base instructions are illegal
candidates.component: Interpreter instruction decoder (interpret-jump-table generated by tools/gen-interpret-jump-table.lua; execute_C_LBU/LHU/LH/SB/SH/ZEXT_B/SEXT_B/ZEXT_H/SEXT_H/ZEXT_W/NOT/MUL); the same decoder is in the uarch program
candidates.role: Honest operator (interpreter). The uarch program, and so the referee verifier's uarch step, are consistent with it
candidates.location: src/interpret.cpp lines ~5268-5390 (Zcb handlers) and ~6126 (dispatch); tools/gen-interpret-jump-table.lua 'Zcb quadrant 0' and following blocks; doc/README.md 'The main processor' ('implements the RV64IMAFDCZicsr_Zifencei ISA'); src/dtb.cpp riscv,isa string built from misa only
candidates.description: The manual documents the ISA as RV64IMAFDCZicsr_Zifencei, and the DTB advertises only misa letters. The emulator also decodes and executes the Zcb compressed instructions (CHANGELOG: 'Added support for RISC-V Zcb compressed instructions'), which the manual never mentions. The encodings Zcb uses are reserved in plain C, for example quadrant-0 funct3=100 (0x8000 is c.lbu s0,0(s0)) and quadrant-1 100111..1x..01, and the spec requires them to raise an illegal-instruction exception. The Zcb spec also makes C.SEXT.B, C.SEXT.H and C.ZEXT.H depend on Zbb, and C.ZEXT.W on Zba. The emulator does not implement Zbb or Zba: sext.b (0x60431293), zext.h (0x080342bb) and add.uw/zext.w (0x080302bb) raise an illegal instruction, while c.sext.b (0x9c65), c.zext.w (0x9c71) and c.zext.h (0x9c69) execute. So the processor implements a combination of extensions that no ratified profile allows, and the manual says nothing about it.
candidates.trigger: Any guest instruction stream that contains one of the Zcb encodings. Software following the manual expects these encodings to trap as illegal instructions.
candidates.reachability: Reachable from any valid template at any privilege level. It is deterministic and consistent across native, uarch and verifier paths, because they share the decoder.
candidates.rating_steps: 1 Out of scope: no. The trigger is guest instructions. 2 Role: the interpreter (Honest operator); no support-only component is involved. 3 High/Medium cases: 'An undocumented deterministic deviation, consistent across all paths, in behavior that no correct guest relies on for isolation or data integrity (R7)' fits: no correct guest is known to rely on these reserved encodings trapping. Claimed: Medium. Also 'A contradiction between the manual and the behavior on a security-relevant point is a defect in one of the two'. Here the manual's ISA statement contradicts the behavior. 4 Critical (alternative reading): R7 lists 'Traps and interrupts' among the areas where 'any deviation lets an input subvert a correct guest'. A reserved encoding that does not raise its illegal-instruction trap is a deviation in that area. Deciding fact: whether some correct guest (for example a trap-and-emulate layer, or a sandbox that relies on illegal-instruction traps) depends on these encodings trapping. 5 Low: n/a.
candidates.threat_to_goal: No path divergence and no wrong hash. R7 requires 'departing only where the manual documents a deviation'. Here the processor departs from the documented ISA, and from the Zcb dependency rules, without documentation. A guest that probes or relies on illegal-instruction traps for these encodings sees behavior the manual does not promise.
candidates.evidence: Differential decode with llvm-mc 18 (-mattr=+m,+a,+f,+d,+c,+zicsr,+zifencei) over all 49,152 16-bit encodings, using probe.lua and cmp.lua in the R7 scratch dir: 1,008 encodings that the emulator executes are invalid for RV64IMAFDC. With +zcb,+zba,+zbb added the mismatch drops to 0. The only remaining emulator-illegal/LLVM-valid encodings are the reserved C.LUI/C.ADDI16SP with imm=0 and 0x0000, where the emulator is correct. zcb.txt shows: 60431293 (sext.b) trap2, 080342bb (zext.h) trap2, 080302bb (zext.w) trap2; 9c65 (c.sext.b) ok, 9c71 (c.zext.w) ok, 9c69 (c.zext.h) ok, 8000 (c.lbu) ok.
candidates.test_idea: bugs/<ID>/test.lua: write each encoding in {0x8000, 0x9c65, 0x9c69, 0x9c71} at the start of RAM of a minimal machine with mtvec set. Run one mcycle in M-mode and assert mcause==2 and pc==mtvec (an illegal-instruction trap, as the documented ISA requires). Alternatively assert that the manual or DTB documents Zcb and that the 32-bit sext.b/zext.h/add.uw execute consistently. The test fails on audit/prt2.

candidates.title: hpmcounter3-31 (0xC03-0xC1F) raise an illegal-instruction exception in M-mode although mhpmcounter3-31 are implemented as read-only zero
candidates.role: Honest operator (interpreter); consistent in the uarch and the verifier
candidates.location: src/interpret.cpp read_csr (~2005-2163): mhpmcounter3..31 return 0, but the hpmcounter3..31 user shadows are absent and fall to the default case (read_csr_fail)
candidates.description: The privileged spec says all mhpmcounter3-31 'should be implemented', and allows them to be read-only zero, which the emulator does. Zihpm defines hpmcounter3-31 as read-only shadows of mhpmcounter3-31. In M-mode, mcounteren does not gate them, so reading hpmcounterN should return 0. The emulator instead raises an illegal-instruction exception for 0xC03-0xC1F at every privilege level. In S/U-mode an exception is correct anyway, because the mcounteren HPM bits are hardwired to 0. The deviation is therefore limited to M-mode reads. The manual does not document it.
candidates.trigger: M-mode guest code (firmware, or any input that took control of the guest) executes csrr t0, hpmcounter3.
candidates.reachability: Reachable from any valid template; deterministic and consistent across paths.
candidates.rating_steps: 1 Out of scope: no. 2 Role: interpreter (Honest operator). 3 Medium case: 'An undocumented deterministic deviation, consistent across all paths, in behavior that no correct guest relies on for isolation or data integrity (R7)'. Reading performance counters is not an isolation or data-integrity mechanism, and OpenSBI probes HPM counters with trap handling. Claimed Medium. If triage judges that implementations without Zihpm may trap here, this is not a defect (Low or none). Deciding fact: whether the emulator claims Zihpm, which it implicitly does by implementing mhpmcounters and mhpmevents. 4 Critical: not applicable, because the behavior is not in an R7-listed area unless 'Traps' is read to cover every spurious illegal-instruction exception. 5 Low: fallback.
candidates.threat_to_goal: None for the goal: no divergence and no wrong hash. It still violates R7's 'implements the RISC-V specification ... departing only where the manual documents a deviation'.
candidates.evidence: An M-mode CSR sweep over all 4096 CSR numbers (csr.txt/csr.out, probe.lua) returned readable sets that include b03..b1f and 320, 323..33f, but not c03..c1f. S-mode and U-mode sweeps with various mcounteren/scounteren settings (probe2.lua) matched the spec.
candidates.test_idea: Run csrrs x5, 0xC03, x0 (0xc03022f3) in M-mode for one mcycle. Assert that no trap occurred and that x5 == 0. The test fails on audit/prt2.

candidates.title: PLIC claim returns the highest pending source ID; the PLIC spec breaks equal-priority ties in favor of the lowest ID
candidates.role: Honest operator (devices), reachable only in unreproducible machines
candidates.description: Every source priority is hardwired to the same level (PLIC_LOWEST_IRQ_PRIORITY). The RISC-V PLIC specification says that among pending sources of equal priority the claim returns the one with the lowest ID. The emulator returns the highest ID (ilog2 of the pending mask). The code never documents this choice, and the manual does not describe PLIC claim ordering.
candidates.trigger: Two or more VirtIO devices raise interrupts at the same time, and the guest claims. Only unreproducible machines have PLIC sources (VirtIO requires iunrep).
candidates.reachability: Not reachable in reproducible machines: girqpend is written only by plic_set_pending_irq, which is called only by VirtIO devices. The configuration rejects VirtIO devices unless iunrep != 0 ('virtio devices are only supported in unreproducible machines'), and girqpend is not guest-writable. No input sequence from a valid template, which is reproducible, can therefore set two pending bits.
candidates.rating_steps: 1 Out of scope: 'Nondeterminism in unreproducible machines (R14)' does not literally cover this, because the behavior is deterministic. R14 places unreproducible machines outside the verifiable domain, however. 2 Role: device (Honest operator), but only in unreproducible machines. 3 Medium/High: no case applies, because it never occurs in a valid template. 4 Critical: no rule is violated at a reachable state of a valid template. 5 Low: 'a real defect that violates no rule or obligation of this model'. Claimed Low.
candidates.threat_to_goal: None: it affects only unreproducible machines. It is reported for completeness as a deviation from the PLIC specification.
candidates.test_idea: In an unreproducible machine with two VirtIO devices, or by setting plic_girqpend through the API to sources 1 and 2, do a 32-bit read of the claim register and assert that it returns 1. The test fails on audit/prt2 (it returns 2).

not_covered: F/D floating-point semantics (softfloat, rounding, NaN-boxing, fflags): read only the FS-off gating; not checked against a reference.

Only sampled the full 32-bit decode space: 327,680 structured encodings (all opcodes x funct3 x funct7 x 5 rs2 values x 2 rd/rs1 pairs) compared with llvm-mc. Rare reserved-field combinations outside this sample were not checked.

Address translation: the permission matrix was tested dynamically only for Sv39 4 KiB leaves (all 256 PTE flag values x U/S/M+MPRV(U,S) x SUM x MXR x load/store/AMO/LR/SC/fetch, 0 mismatches against a spec model). Sv48, superpages (including misaligned superpages), non-leaf reserved bits, PBMT/N bits, and PTEs outside RAM were not tested dynamically; I only read the code.

Exception delegation (medeleg) and exception priority ordering were not tested dynamically. Interrupt delegation and priority were tested exhaustively for the 6 standard bits x mie x mideleg x prv x MIE/SIE (393,216 cases, 0 mismatches).
Did not run the uarch, uarch replay or regenerated Solidity step to confirm that the candidates behave identically on those paths. I relied on the shared interpret.cpp source.
TLB hot/cold slot verification, replay-step TLB handling and stale-translation reproduction (R10/R2) were not covered.
Stop/resume boundaries for interrupts and timer ticks (R2) were not covered beyond reading interpret_loop.

Guest software: I read libcmt (io.c, rollup.c, abi.c, buf.c, merkle.c) at v0.18.1-test1 and found no defect. I did not cover rollup-http-server (Rust), the rollup CLI, io-mock, or the higher-level language bindings. The Linux cmio driver is out of scope.

Did not report: a failed SC sets the PTE D bit on a TLB miss (the Svadu spec's 'D updates must be exact' may or may not cover failing SCs); zero PMP entries (pmpcfg/pmpaddr CSRs trap in M-mode); CLINT faults on 32-bit mtimecmp accesses, 64-bit msip accesses and mtime writes (I could not confirm a spec requirement offline).
HTIF console getchar and VirtIO paths (unreproducible only), and the PLIC/SEIP conflation that the code comment documents, were not assessed further.
